title: Two Vegan Burritos at Contrasting Budgets: Gluten-Based Seitan versus Premium Impossible Meat
summary: Goodful contrasts a budget-friendly vegan burrito with a premium option, challenging the cooks to produce two burritos at different price points and have a judge determine value. The cheaper burrito centers on a gluten-based seitan made from all-purpose flour, including kneading to develop gluten, resting, washing to remove starch, seasoning, and forming a knot before searing and simmering in a flavored liquid. The more expensive burrito features Impossible Meat cooked with onions and spices, plus a roasted poblano cashew crema and a fresh guacamole, assembled across two tortillas for a larger, “beefy” burrito. Preparations emphasize plant-based techniques such as gluten development and washing, spice blends, sauce-building with silken tofu as a faux cashew crema, and budget-conscious pantry choices (rice, pinto beans, salsa, lettuce). Jasmine serves as the taste-test judge to compare flavor, texture, and overall value between the $1.50 burrito and the $14 burrito.
topics: spice blending for seitan (salt, garlic powder, cumin, chili powder, black pepper, oregano)
seitan marinade (water, soy sauce, orange juice, lime juice)
guacamole with lime, tomato, red onion, jalapeño
budget burrito assembly (romaine, salsa, rice, pinto beans, corn)
taste test and value judgment by Jasmine

sections.title: Introduction and challenge setup
sections.description: The hosts introduce the challenge: build two vegan burritos at different price points ($1.50 vs $14) and have Jasmine judge which offers the best value.

sections.title: Budget vs premium approach and seitan direction
sections.description: One host commits to a $1.50 burrito using gluten-based seitan from all-purpose flour, while noting the other burrito will take a higher-budget approach.

sections.title: Gluten development and resting
sections.description: The process begins with mixing all-purpose flour and water, kneading to develop gluten, and resting the dough before gluten-washing steps begin.

sections.title: Gluten washing and seasoning setup
concepts: seasoning the gluten ball (salt, garlic powder, cumin, chili powder, black pepper, oregano)
sections.description: The gluten is washed to remove starch, then seasoned heavily to resemble meat-flavored seitan.

sections.title: Flavoring and resting the gluten ball
sections.description: The seasoned gluten ball rests to let the spices infuse before further shaping.

sections.title: Shaping and searing the gluten for texture
sections.description: The gluten is twisted into a knot-like form, then seared in oil to develop a golden crust.

sections.title: Budget burrito assembly prep
sections.description: Base burrito components are prepared for assembly, including vegetables and inexpensive proteins.

sections.title: Premium burrito prep: Impossible Meat introduction
sections.description: The other burrito uses Impossible Meat with onions and a spice profile to emulate meat texture.

sections.title: Crema and guacamole foundations
sections.description: A silk-based crema substitutes cashews, paired with a roasted poblano crema and a fresh guacamole.

sections.title: Burrito assembly (premium option emphasizes volume and cheese)
sections.description: The premium burrito is assembled on dual tortillas with abundant fillings and vegan cheese for a hearty finish.

sections.title: Taste test and value judgment
sections.description: Jasmine tastes both burritos and discusses flavor, texture, and whether the budget version delivers value compared to the premium option.

sections.title: Wrap-up and outro
sections.description: The host discusses the outcome, closing remarks, and tease for future videos.
